project.name: INCIDENT ATTACK
project.subtitle: Red Team vs Blue Team — Cybersecurity Awareness Game
project.event: Security Week, fictional LNG company context
project.purpose: Interactive, accessible two-player security-awareness booth experience that teaches how attacker choices, SOC alert prioritization, and delayed response affect data exposure and business consequences.

statuses.implemented: Present in latest V5.1 source files and offline demonstration.
statuses.requested_future: Discussed, but not part of V5.1 or not yet fully specified.
statuses.superseded: Earlier approach replaced by current design.
statuses.recommended: Developer recommendation, not a user-approved requirement.

red.objective: Build a convincing phishing campaign, gain access, distract the SOC, and extract target data.
red.turn_action: Select 1 main attack and 1 distraction, then launch.
red.visual_theme: Red/dark, masked hooded hacker character, sirens as attempts are stopped.

blue.objective: Protect the simulated company by handling urgent real threats before misleading/noisy signals.
blue.turn_action: Tap 3 fixed-position SIEM alert cards to assign order 1, 2, 3. Submission triggers automatic containment/handling — NO extra response choices.
blue.visual_theme: Blue/dark, Omani SOC analyst in dishdasha and kumma, matrix-style code grows with data loss.

devices.actual_event: Two laptop browsers connected to same local Node server
devices.demo: One browser showing Red and Blue simultaneously in split-screen; game state shared, not two unrelated demos
devices.spectator: Optional spectator role in multiplayer build

core_experience.remaining_time_usage: Intro, transitions, cinematic final reveal, and player handover; not a server-enforced 6-minute hard stop.
flow: Red chooses a main tactic and a distraction
Blue receives 3 generated simulated SIEM alerts immediately
Blue taps alert cards in urgency order
Game automatically resolves the whole queue and updates results/state
Next round starts, through all 4 rounds
Final grades, outcome, real-world case study, replay
core_experience.simple_copy_target: Most on-screen descriptions understood in approximately 2–3 seconds; avoid technical jargon unless explained in debrief.

source_mix: 1 Red-selected distraction, which may be dangerous, ambiguous, or legitimate
alert_generation.red_visibility: Red sees own two selections; does not get Blue cards or their best ordering ahead of time.
alert_generation.blue_visibility: Blue sees title, description, icon, visible severity label, and concise evidence clue; not the hidden true priority, correct engine outcome, or which event was the main attack.
alert_generation.severity_vs_urgency: Visible severity is deliberately NOT a reliable ranking. A CRITICAL approved backup or scan may have hidden priority 1, while a lower labeled incident might be the real risk.
alert_generation.deterministic_permutation: Main, side, ambient are shown in a stage/choice dependent permutation, so attacker identity is not revealed by card position.
alert_generation.rank_interaction: Click/tap to add #1, then #2, then #3 to existing stationary cards. Click an assigned card again to remove its rank. Do not reorder or physically move cards; no extra STOP/VERIFY/IGNORE buttons.
alert_generation.submit_requirement: Three distinct alert IDs ranked; engine refuses incomplete or duplicate rankings.
alert_generation.timeout_behavior: If Blue times out, engine uses current display order as fallback. If Red times out, engine uses the first primary and first distraction option.

outcomes_and_scoring.valuation_status: Fictional risk/exposure scoring currency; NOT real corporate asset value, actual cash stolen, dark-web market price, or validated monetary loss.

incident_outcomes.titles_by_magnitude: PARTIAL DATA BREACH until under 60%; MAJOR DATA BREACH from 60% through 99%

triage.priority_definition: Each alert has a hidden integer priority and the ideal order is descending priority.
triage.pairwise_scoring: For each of the three pairs among the three alerts, a point is awarded if the higher-urgency item was placed before the lower-urgency item. Equal priorities are not penalized.
triage.delay_rule: Only lower-priority events placed before an actionable threat create a missed containment window. Prioritizing a more urgent threat first does not penalize handling the other later.
triage.normal_handling: All three events are automatically handled in ranked order; no extra choices after ranking.
triage.threat_resolution: A correct=stop threat handled without a lower-priority precursor is contained before it leaks. Delayed stop threats can leak proportional to their configured leak value (rounds 3–4). Verify/leave events are not treated as leaks just because they were displayed.
triage.actionable_alert_leak_calculation: ceil(alert.leak * delay_rate), summed across applicable events, with final-round adjustments and a cap at 100% total.
triage.disruption_interpretation: Illustrative attention/wasted-triage cost (from V3), not actual invoice costs or a universal cost for checking legitimate events.

final_round_adjustments.multiplier: 0.70 + min(0.55, accumulated_compromise / 100), applied to round 4 preliminary extracted amount; then ceil and cap to remaining dataset.
final_round_adjustments.rare_complete_loss_cascade: An actual 100% result is possible only with accumulated prior exposure, >=6 prior priority mistakes, a high-pressure campaign, and the final Red choices "large" + "forward" both handled late; see engine.js resolve() for the exact guard.
final_round_adjustments.exact_engine_condition: stage===3 && extracted_before_round4>=12 && total_priorityMistakes_before_round4>=6 && pendingRed.primary==='large' && pendingRed.side==='forward' && main.queue===3 && main.wasDelayed && side.wasDelayed && compromise>=18

financial_report_fields.response_disruption: sum of simulated triage overhead costs
financial_report_fields.disclaimer: All figures illustrative, not real LNG prices, criminal profit or measured business losses.

blue_grade.S: 0% extracted AND 12/12 triage points AND 0 priority mistakes

outcomes_and_scoring.best_practice: Protect scoreboard correctness by keeping resolution in authoritative game engine/server. Screen animations must not change damage or score.

demo_only_animation.red_launch: Glowing attack/comet travels from Red side and slams into Blue panel with impact flash.
demo_only_animation.blue_resolution: Blue shield dome wraps visible Blue panel when its ordered response is submitted.

matrix_effects.ambient_blue_rain: More columns and higher opacity as confirmed extractedPercent increases; not a claim that encryption is happening.
matrix_effects.blue_clock_scramble: During Blue turn, glyphs progressively scramble with elapsed time as a separate tension effect, and status may say WATCHING LIVE, SYSTEM UNDER THREAT or BREACH IN PROGRESS.
matrix_effects.red_siren: Flashing red-blue light rises with number of main attack attempts stopped.

visual_audio_ux.audio_implementation: Browser Web Audio oscillator-based effects; user gesture initializes audio; sound on/off toggle; browser autoplay policies apply.

final_cinematic.intent: Do not reveal result immediately after last Blue submission; show both teams processing outcome first.
final_cinematic.overlay: Red: cash settlement/loading. Blue: Matrix digits/decrypting incident report. Then grades and report.
final_cinematic.v5_1_red_value_fix: Final cash amount is visually hidden with CSS until near the end of the loading animation; it performs approximately 10 brief randomized display ticks, then settles on the true amount. Final results appear only afterward.
final_cinematic.important: The randomized rolling digits are purely visual and must NEVER alter actual final money, extracted %, or grading.

real_world_case_studies.design_intent: Link the final outcome to a credible, related real cyber incident with a lesson; avoid misleading claims of exact equivalence or LNG data market prices.

existing_examples_from_engine.outcome_use: 0%-35% extracted (with different text for 0% vs nonzero)

Approximately US$100 million negative impact on adjusted property EBITDAR from September 2023 disruption, a distinct real case; NOT a value estimate for fictional LNG theft.

real_world_case_studies.production_note: Reverify source links and exact wording before external/public display.

offline_solo.launch: Extract project or download standalone HTML; open PLAY-OFFLINE-SOLO.html in Edge/Chrome; choose Live split-screen demo; start.
offline_solo.behavior: Two team panes share one in-browser engine state.

LAN_multiplayer.storage: Rooms are in server RAM; browser stores role/token in sessionStorage. No persistent database.
notes: Both devices need network access to host IP and chosen port.
This is a demonstration server, not a hardened production deployment.
SSE auth uses query token; use TLS, stronger session architecture, and audited hosting for a public event.

API.description: Create room, assign Red host credentials.
Subscribe to refresh notifications using SSE.

request_payload_examples.note: The three e1/e2/e3 keys are assigned to generated alerts, and display order is shuffled; submit IDs in player selected sequence.

technical_architecture.security_disclaimer: Simulation only: no phishing emails sent, no credential capture, no exploit execution, and no actual file exfiltration.

testing.v5_1_verification: 12/12 Node automated tests passed after fixing shield alignment and money-reveal behavior.
test_scenarios: Four mandatory rounds even after early successful defense
Wrong alert order causes measurable late-response harm
Perfect Blue ordering prevents all extraction
One late response cannot instantly cause full loss
limitations: This test count does not prove every browser size/device was manually reviewed after V5.1.
Usability and game balance need real participant testing.

changes: Proposed two-laptop, two-player Red vs Blue turn-based competition for Security Week.
Attack selection plus defensive reaction, multiple-choice language that any employee understands quickly.
30-second turn, under-six-minute total event target; total fictional LNG assets with no, partial, or complete extraction; end grades and real incident facts.
Initial phishing proof-of-concept had 4 attack/defense stages and explicit Blue response choices like block, investigate, ignore.
Early containment could make Blue too strong and matches end without much gameplay.
Red gained primary attack plus distractions and three simultaneous SIEM events.
Blue sorted events and chose separate block/check/ignore actions (six actions total).
Overreaction/wasted time penalties.
Four rounds guaranteed.
Removed all Blue action buttons; Blue ONLY orders three alerts.
Severity intentionally differs from urgency; ranking delays drive data loss.
Fixed visible numbered picks rather than excessive decisions.
Sound effects, screen flashes, Blue Matrix theme and Red failed-attack sirens.
Offline solo split-screen shows simultaneous Red/Blue views and immediate Red-to-Blue alerts.
Blue data-rain grows with real game loss.
Cinematic final loading/score reveal for both sides.
Full 100% data extraction made attainable in rare extreme bad-defense scenario.
Side roadmap with 2 planning rounds and 2 attack rounds, hiding extraction until it can actually occur.
Static Blue alert cards gain rank numbers; no card reshuffle after selection.
Animated Red hooded attacker and Blue Omani analyst, idle and typing GIFs; optional cosmetic appearances.
Demo-only Red projectile crashing into Blue and Blue shield effect.
Blue shield dome aligned to visible Blue content panel using element bounds/inset and centered insignia.
Red cinematic final amount hidden during loading, then animated random digit roll, ending on true amount before score display.
Existing engine and server tests still pass (12/12).
